ble_219_0c045940.name: ble_i2c_write_read_locked
ble_219_0c045940.summary: Run one I2C write-then-read under a per-instance mutex; returns the read length

The instance index is the u16 that param_1+0x10 points to, and the transaction runs under the static mutex at 0x2000F2B4 + instance*0x50 (taken with an infinite timeout through FUN_0C0430A8 and released through FUN_0C042C8C). hal_i2c_recv traps for instance 6 and above, so a bad index hangs the firmware instead of returning an error. On success the function returns the read length from descriptor byte 2; otherwise it returns the non-zero error of the failed phase. It has no direct callers, so it is reached through a callback or table.

params.name: param_1
params.description: context struct; the u16 instance index is at the pointer stored at +0x10

params.name: param_2
params.description: I2C request: u8 address @0, u8 write length @1, u8 read length @2, write buffer pointer @4, read buffer pointer @8

returns.description: read length (descriptor byte 2) on success, else the non-zero hal_i2c error

ble_219_0c045940.notes: FUN_0C0430A8 and FUN_0C042C8C are not yet described; their take/give roles are inferred from the 0x50-byte per-instance record stride.

ble_219_0c045d60.name: ble_app_block16_f36c_read

The 16-byte bound comes from the 0x11 comparison, and the block contents are not identified here. Callers are at 0x0C02A484, 0x0C02B158 and 0x0C02CCA8.

Callers are at 0x0C02CCA8, 0x0C058160, 0x0C058170, 0x0C0581A8 and 0x0C058250.

ble_219_0c045e74.name: ble_app_block40_f38c_read
ble_219_0c045e74.summary: Copy the 40-byte app block at 0x2000F38C..0x2000F3B3, gated by request 0x101
ble_219_0c045e74.description: Gated snapshot of a 40-byte RAM block: ten consecutive 32-bit words from 0x2000F38C to 0x2000F3B0 are copied in order into the caller's buffer, after the app device request 0x101 (FUN_0C041E10) has succeeded. ble_219_0c045f04.summary: Report whether the marker byte at 0x2000F36A is 'S', gated by request 0x101

ble_219_0c045f60.name: ble_app_magic_caf_check
ble_219_0c045f60.summary: Check the 32-bit magic 0x00464143 ('CAF') at 0x2000F3B4, gated by request 0x101

ble_219_0c0460e8.name: ble_spi_read_locked
ble_219_0c0460e8.summary: Receive-only SPI transfer on the active record, with try-lock and format reapply
ble_219_0c0460e8.description: Clocks param_1[1] bytes in from SPI, sending zeros, and stores them at param_2. The request's u16 at +0 selects a 12-byte flag record at 0x20003EE8; if its bits 3 or 4 are set they are cleared and FUN_0C032714 finishes the previous operation. The active SPI record is chosen by the byte at 0x2000391E (20-byte stride from 0x20003920), and the function try-locks 0x20003D05 through the ROM patch thunk at 0x200007F4, returning 0xFFFFFFE1 when the lock is busy. It reapplies that record's format with hal_spi_apply_format, and spins forever if the record's flags byte at +0x0B has its low two bits set (a trap, not an error return). Otherwise it calls hal_spi_txrx_poll with a NULL transmit buffer, restores the format with the saved low bits, and unlocks through the thunk at 0x2000081C.

params.name: param_1
params.description: request: u16 channel index at +0, u16 byte count at +2

returns.description: 0 on success; otherwise the hal_spi_txrx_poll status (1 early end, -1 bad length, -11 SPI busy), or -31 when the lock is busy

ble_219_0c0460e8.notes: The SPI instance passed to the transfer is not recovered by the decompiler (it shows the r0 left by the format call); the format call uses instance 1. The infinite loop is an assertion-style trap. FUN_0C032714 and the two ROM-patch thunks are not yet described.

ble_219_0c046494.name: ble_uart_port_start
ble_219_0c046494.summary: Start UART port 0..2: 115200-baud config, IRQ handler install and RX interrupt enable

It fills the 24-byte port record at 0x2000F414 + index*0x18 with the four-word line config {0x00030000, 0x00000201, 0x0001C200, 0} (0x1C200 is 115200 baud), stores 0x7C0 at +0x10 and the context pointer param_1 at +0x14, and clears two u16 counters at +4 and +6 of the port descriptor. The config goes to FUN_0C034008, the port's IRQ number is read from the table at 0x0C076850 and installed with hal_irq_install_handler (the context pointer is passed as the handler slot value), and the UART interrupt mask is then written through hal_uart_set_irq_mask. The decompiler does not recover the mask argument, so the value written is unknown.

params.name: param_1
params.description: request struct; the pointer at +0x10 leads to the port descriptor, whose first u16 is the port index (0..2)

returns.description: 0, or -19 (-ENODEV) for a bad port index

ble_219_0c046494.notes: The 115200 baud reading of 0x1C200 is an inference. FUN_0C034008 is not yet described.

ble_219_0c046a58.name: ble_vendor_fc87_send_keyed
ble_219_0c046a58.summary: Send vendor HCI 0xFC87 for the table record whose key matches request byte 7
ble_219_0c046a58.description: Runs FUN_0C03BD70 and then sends a 32-byte vendor HCI command, opcode 0xFC87 with a 28-byte parameter block, built from the 8-byte request in param_1: byte 0 goes to parameter 6, bytes 1 to 6 (an address) fill parameters 8 to 13, and byte 7 is a key. The key is matched against the first byte of the 27 six-byte records at 0x20003EF0; parameters 15, 16 and 18-19 take that record's byte 2, byte 1 and u16 at +4. The fixed parts are parameters 0-3 = 01 E8 03 00, parameter 7 = 0x02, parameter 14 = 0x01, parameter 17 = 0x04 and parameters 24-27 = 0xFFFFFFFF, with 4-5 and 20-23 zero. A missing key returns -1 without sending; on a match the counters at 0x2000F468 and 0x2000F46C are cleared when set, and the frame goes out through FUN_0C03AC98 with length 32.

params.name: param_1
params.description: 8-byte request: [0] parameter byte, [1..6] address, [7] record key

returns.description: 0 when a matching record was sent, -1 when no record has the key

ble_219_0c046a58.notes: Field meanings (the 0xFC87 command, the 0x03E8 word, the 27-record table) are inferred from the parameter layout. The constant sibling ble_vendor_fc87_send_test_pattern is the cross-check. FUN_0C03AC98 and FUN_0C03BD70 are not yet described.

ble_219_0c046af0.name: ble_vendor_fc87_send_test_pattern
ble_219_0c046af0.summary: Send the fixed vendor HCI 0xFC87 test frame with a 0x55 address field
ble_219_0c046af0.description: Takes no input and sends one fixed 32-byte frame: vendor opcode 0xFC87, parameter length 28, and parameters 02 E8 03 00 | 00 00 00 02 | 55 55 55 55 55 55 | 01 01 | 04 04 36 00 | 00 00 00 00 | FF FF FF FF. It is the keyed frame of ble_vendor_fc87_send_keyed with the address field filled with 0x55 bytes, mode byte 0x02 instead of the keyed 0x01, and the table fields set to constants (0x0036 at parameters 18-19). The 0x55 payload and the test-style layout suggest a non-signalling TX or test configuration, which is an inference. It calls only FUN_0C03AC98, without FUN_0C03BD70.

returns.description: always 0

ble_219_0c046af0.notes: Caller is ble_219_0c02c49c, which also calls the keyed sender and the LE test commands.

ble_219_0c046b4c.name: ble_hci_le_tx_test_cmd
ble_219_0c046b4c.summary: Send HCI LE Transmitter Test (0x201E) with channel, length and payload type
ble_219_0c046b4c.description: Sends the 7-byte HCI command 01 1E 20 03 p0 p1 p2, which is LE Transmitter Test (opcode 0x201E, three parameters): TX_Channel = p0, Length_of_Test_Data = p1 and Packet_Payload = p2, all taken from the 3-byte request in param_1. It runs FUN_0C03BD70 first and clears the test-state word at 0x2000F464 when it is non-zero, then hands the frame to FUN_0C03AC98. It always returns 0.

params.name: param_1

returns.description: always 0

ble_219_0c046b4c.notes: The opcode mapping follows the Bluetooth Core LE Test command set. FUN_0C03AC98 (the HCI send) and FUN_0C03BD70 are not yet described.

ble_219_0c046b90.name: ble_hci_le_rx_test_cmd
ble_219_0c046b90.summary: Send HCI LE Receiver Test (0x201D) with one RX channel byte
ble_219_0c046b90.description: Sends the 5-byte HCI command 01 1D 20 01 p0, which is LE Receiver Test (opcode 0x201D) with RX_Channel = p0 taken from the 1-byte request. It runs FUN_0C03BD70 first, then FUN_0C03AC98 with length 5, and always returns 0. It is the receive-side counterpart of ble_hci_le_tx_test_cmd.

ble_219_0c046bbc.summary: Send HCI LE Enhanced Transmitter Test (0x2034) with four parameter bytes
ble_219_0c046bbc.description: Sends the 8-byte HCI command 01 34 20 04 followed by the four bytes at param_1, which is LE Enhanced Transmitter Test (opcode 0x2034): TX_Channel, Test_Data_Length, Packet_Payload and PHY, in that order. It runs FUN_0C03BD70 first, then FUN_0C03AC98, and always returns 0. The fourth parameter (PHY) is what distinguishes it from ble_hci_le_tx_test_cmd.

ble_219_0c046bfc.name: ble_hci_le_enh_rx_test_cmd
ble_219_0c046bfc.summary: Send HCI LE Enhanced Receiver Test (0x2033) with three parameter bytes
ble_219_0c046bfc.description: Sends the 7-byte HCI command 01 33 20 03 p0 p1 p2, which is LE Enhanced Receiver Test (opcode 0x2033): RX_Channel, PHY and Modulation_Index, from the 3-byte request. It runs FUN_0C03BD70 first, then FUN_0C03AC98, and always returns 0.

ble_219_0c046c34.name: ble_hci_le_test_end_cmd

Unlike the other test-command senders it does not call FUN_0C03BD70 first. The controller's reply, which carries the received-packet count in the Bluetooth spec, is handled elsewhere.

returns.description: always 0

ble_219_0c046e88.name: ble_stack_lock_take
ble_219_0c046e88.summary: Take the shared BLE stack mutex, creating it on first use while the scheduler runs
ble_219_0c046e88.description: Creates the mutex lazily: if the handle at 0x2000F4C0 is NULL, FUN_0C042D80 is called with type 4 (presumed FreeRTOS recursive mutex) and the static 80-byte buffer at 0x2000F470, and the function returns if creation fails. Otherwise, when xTaskGetSchedulerState reports anything but 0 (suspended), the mutex is taken with an infinite timeout through FUN_0C0431F8. Nothing is taken while the scheduler is suspended, and ble_stack_lock_give applies the same test on release. Callers at 0x0C070F40, 0x0C070FD8 and 0x0C071080 use it around shared BLE stack code.

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c046e88.notes: The type code 4 and the FUN_0C0431F8 take are inferred from the other uses in this packet (for example the streaming buffer in ble_pktq_enqueue).

ble_219_0c046ec0.name: ble_stack_lock_give
ble_219_0c046ec0.summary: Release the shared BLE stack mutex taken by ble_stack_lock_take
ble_219_0c046ec0.description: Gives the mutex at handle 0x2000F4C0 through FUN_0C042DF4 when the handle is non-NULL and xTaskGetSchedulerState is not 0 (not suspended), mirroring the take. It does nothing when the mutex was never created or the scheduler is suspended, so a scheduler suspension between take and give leaves the mutex held; that case is not handled.

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c047588.name: ble_byte_count_notify
ble_219_0c047588.summary: Add a byte count to a running total and fire the registered notify callback
ble_219_0c047588.description: If the optional count hook at 0x2000F60C is set, it is called with no arguments and its return value replaces the count. A positive count is added to the 32-bit running total at 0x2000F644, and if the listener record at 0x2000F64C has a callback at +4, the function evaluates total*1000 divided by the value at 0x2000F648 through __divdi3 (FUN_0C06FE20) and then calls that callback with no arguments. The quotient is not used in the decompiled code, so either the division is dead or the decompile is incomplete. The function returns the possibly replaced count.

params.name: param_1
params.description: not used by the decompiled body

params.name: param_2
params.description: byte count; replaced by the hook result when the hook is set

returns.description: the count after the optional hook

ble_219_0c048278.name: ble_evt_set_index_bit
ble_219_0c048278.summary: Set event bit 2*index + (selector & 1) in the BLE event group at 0x2000F6D4
ble_219_0c048278.description: Maps an index and a selector to one bit of the event group at 0x2000F6D4: bit = 2*index + (selector & 1), with mask = 1 << bit. A mask of zero (bit 32 or more) skips the call. Otherwise it calls FUN_0C04291C with the group and the mask, presumed to be xEventGroupSetBits and the counterpart of the xEventGroupClearBits used by ble_evt_clear_index_bit. The even/odd layout is the one ble_fd_select uses: write readiness on the even bit and read readiness on the odd bit of descriptor index fd-3. Callers are at 0x0C0462C4 and 0x0C046380.

params.name: param_2
params.description: selector: bit 0 set means read readiness, clear means write readiness

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c048298.name: ble_evt_clear_index_bit
ble_219_0c048298.summary: Clear the event bit that ble_evt_set_index_bit sets, via xEventGroupClearBits
ble_219_0c048298.description: Uses the same index and selector mapping as ble_evt_set_index_bit and clears that bit in the event group at 0x2000F6D4 with FUN_0C042900, which is xEventGroupClearBits per its annotation. It returns immediately when the mask is zero. Callers are at 0x0C0422D4, 0x0C0424D8 and 0x0C04264C, which presumably consume a readiness event.

params.name: param_2
params.description: selector: bit 0 set means read readiness, clear means write readiness

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c0482b8.name: ble_evt_read_bits
ble_219_0c0482b8.summary: Return the whole BLE event group value when the index bit is valid, else 0
ble_219_0c0482b8.description: Returns 0 when the event group handle at 0x2000F6D4 is NULL or when the index's mask is zero. Otherwise it returns the result of FUN_0C042988 on the group (a one-argument call, presumed xEventGroupGetBits), which is the full group value and not only the requested bit, so callers must mask the result. Callers are at 0x0C04533C, 0x0C0462C4, 0x0C046380 and 0x0C0467B8.

returns.description: whole event group value, or 0

ble_219_0c0484f0.name: ble_fd_find_next_open
ble_219_0c0484f0.summary: Find the next open descriptor above param_1 (numbers 3..48), or return -1
ble_219_0c0484f0.description: Scans the descriptor table at 0x2000F6D8 (one pointer per descriptor, 46 entries for descriptor numbers 3..48, non-NULL meaning open) for the first open descriptor numbered above param_1. It returns -1 when param_1 is below 2 or when nothing open follows. The scan runs under the mutex at 0x2000F680, which is created on first use with FUN_0C042D80(1, 0x2000F684) and taken with a 100-tick timeout whose result is not checked, then released with FUN_0C042C8C. params.name: param_1
params.description: current descriptor number; the search starts at the next number

returns.description: next open descriptor number, or -1

ble_219_0c04885c.name: ble_fd_select
ble_219_0c04885c.summary: POSIX-style select() over descriptors 3..maxfd, waiting on the BLE event group
ble_219_0c04885c.description: Implements select(maxfd, readfds, writefds, exceptfds, timeout) for descriptors 3 to maxfd; exceptfds is ignored. The timeout is converted to milliseconds (NULL means wait forever), and when either set is given with maxfd above 2, each requested descriptor adds one bit to the event mask (2*(fd-3) for write, 2*(fd-3)+1 for read) that FUN_0C042858 waits on. A descriptor in range with no ops pointer sets errno to EBADF (9) and returns -1. When the wait is satisfied, both caller sets are cleared and each requested descriptor whose bit fired has the readiness method at offset 0x10 of its ops object called (bit 1 readable, bit 0 writable); the caller's bit is set and the return value is the number of bits set. A timeout returns 0 without clearing the sets, which differs from POSIX, and when nothing was requested the function delays for the timeout (FUN_0C0441A8) and returns 0.

params.name: param_1
params.description: maxfd, the highest descriptor number checked

params.name: param_2
params.description: readfds bitmap, one bit per descriptor in u32 words

params.name: param_5
params.description: timeout: s32 seconds at +0 and microseconds at +8; NULL waits forever

returns.description: number of ready descriptor bits; 0 on timeout or nothing requested; -1 with errno EBADF; or the negative status of a readiness method

ble_219_0c04885c.notes: Caller is ble_219_0c02eb60. The readiness method is called without visible arguments because the decompiler drops them. FUN_0C042858, FUN_0C0441A8 and FUN_0C0701F8 (__errno) are referenced; the first two are not yet described.

ble_219_0c0489e8.name: ble_pktq_init
ble_219_0c0489e8.summary: Initialise a packet ring of n+1 descriptor slots and create its recursive mutex

The creation result is not checked.

params.name: param_2

params.name: param_3
params.description: 4-byte aligned storage of at least (8 + slot_size) * (n+1) bytes

params.name: param_4
params.description: not used by the initialiser; passed through to the mutex creator

ble_219_0c048a44.name: ble_pktq_enqueue
ble_219_0c048a44.summary: Append a packet to the ble_pktq ring: copy the payload into the next slot

returns.description: 0 on success, 14 if the payload is oversized, 16 if the ring is full

ble_219_0c04920c.name: ble_sha1_mix_pair16

params.description: 16-byte input B, or NULL for the built-in constant

ble_219_0c04aa80.name: ble_sha1_oneshot

ble_219_0c04aa80.description: Clears a 92-byte mbedTLS SHA-1 context with memset and loads the standard IV (0x67452301, 0xEFCDAB89, 0x98BADCFE, 0x10325476, 0xC3D2E1F0). It feeds the input through mbedtls_sha1_update_ret when the length is non-zero and writes the 20-byte digest through mbedtls_sha1_finish_ret. The finish is skipped when the update fails, so the output is then left untouched. The context is zeroed byte by byte before returning.

params.name: param_2
params.description: input length in bytes; 0 is allowed

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c04aae8.name: ble_sha1_oneshot_thunk
ble_219_0c04aae8.description: A single-instruction branch to ble_sha1_oneshot at 0x0C04AA80; Ghidra shows the target body here. Arguments pass through unchanged, so the behaviour is that of ble_sha1_oneshot. Its only caller in this packet is ble_sha1_mix_pair16.

params.name: param_1
params.description: input data pointer, as in ble_sha1_oneshot

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c04af54.name: hid_report_size_valid
ble_219_0c04af54.summary: BTstack hid_report_size_valid(): check a report size against boot rules or the HID descriptor
ble_219_0c04af54.description: Entry of BTstack hid_report_size_valid(cid, report_id, report_type, size). The first three instructions reject size 0, and the rest is the body at 0x0C04AF5A. For the boot-protocol device (cid equal to DAT_2000FA10 and protocol-mode byte DAT_2000FA2A equal to 0), report ID 1 (keyboard) needs size 8 or more, report ID 2 (mouse) at least 1, and any other ID fails. A cid mismatch logs 'hid_device_in_boot_protocol_mode: could not find hid device instace' (hid_device.c line 0x3D6) through ble_hook_invoke_indexed and falls through. Otherwise the size must equal btstack_hid_get_report_size_for_id(report_id, report_type, DAT_2000FA0C, DAT_2000FA08) exactly, and a zero result fails.

params.name: param_4
params.description: report size in bytes, non-zero on entry

returns.description: true when the size is valid for that report

ble_219_0c04af54.notes: Entry split: the body is hid_report_size_valid_body (ble_219_0c04af5a), which carries the same logic; the split is a Ghidra artefact.

ble_219_0c04afcc.name: hid_device_validate_report
ble_219_0c04afcc.summary: Check an outgoing HID report's report ID and size against the device's descriptor
ble_219_0c04afcc.description: Checks a report about to be sent on device cid (param_1) with report type param_2 and length param_3, whose bytes are at param_4. If the descriptor declares report IDs (btstack_hid_report_id_declared on DAT_2000FA0C and DAT_2000FA08), the first byte is the report ID: an INVALID ID (hid_report_id_status returns 2) gives result 2 at once, and one byte is removed from the length. Without declared IDs the report ID is 0. The size is then validated by hid_report_size_valid (0x0C04AF54), and a failure returns 4.

params.name: param_3
params.description: report length, including the report ID byte when IDs are declared

returns.description: 0 when valid, 2 for an invalid report ID, 4 for a bad size

ble_219_0c04afcc.notes: The function that transmits the report is not in this packet, and the name is ours.

ble_219_0c04b788.name: hid_create_sdp_record
ble_219_0c04b788.summary: Build the HID device SDP service record into a data-element buffer
ble_219_0c04b788.description: Writes the complete HID device SDP service record into the data-element buffer at param_1 with the BTstack sdp_util builders. Attributes emitted: 0x0000 record handle (param_2), 0x0001 service class 0x1124 (HID), 0x0004 protocol list L2CAP plus HIDP (PSM 0x11), 0x0006 language base (en, UTF-8, base 0x0100), 0x0009 profile descriptor (HID version 0x0101), 0x000D additional protocol list with L2CAP PSM 0x13 (interrupt channel), and 0x0100 the service name, read as a pointer and strlen from the parameter block. The HID attributes are 0x0201 parser version 0x0111, 0x0202 subclass (u16 at byte 0), 0x0203 country code (byte 2), 0x0204 virtual cable (byte 3), 0x0205 reconnect initiate (byte 5), 0x020A remote wake (byte 4), 0x020C supervision timeout (u16 at byte 12), 0x020D normally connectable (byte 6), 0x020E boot device (byte 7), 0x020F and 0x0210 SSR latency and timeout (u16 at bytes 8 and 10), and 0x0206 the report descriptor as a type-0x22 element with pointer at byte 16 and length at byte 20.

params.name: param_1
params.description: output buffer for the data elements

params.name: param_3
params.description: HID configuration block; byte offsets are given in the description

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c04b788.notes: The name follows the upstream BTstack builder name from memory; no SDP string in the export confirms it. Offsets are byte offsets within the parameter block.

ble_219_0c04bb00.name: hid_device_init
ble_219_0c04bb00.summary: Store the HID report descriptor and callbacks, then register HID PSMs 0x11 and 0x13
ble_219_0c04bb00.description: Stores the report descriptor length (u16 param_2, to 0x2000FA0C) and pointer (param_3, to 0x2000FA08), stores the u8 param_1 at 0x2000F9FC, and installs three handler pointers 0x0C04AEF0, 0x0C04AEFC and 0x0C04AEF8 (Thumb bit set) at 0x20003F9C, 0x20003FA0 and 0x20003FA4. It then registers the HID control PSM 0x11 and the interrupt PSM 0x13 with l2cap_register_service, each with MTU 100 and the security level from ble_ctrl_env_get_mode_or_4 (0x0C066EE4), using the fixed handler context LAB_0C04B01C. The arguments match the descriptor-length and descriptor parameters of BTstack hid_device_init() as far as known; the extra u8 parameter is not explained. The caller is 0x0C058F00.

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c04bd48.name: sdp_init
ble_219_0c04bd48.summary: Register the SDP server on PSM 1 with MTU 0xFFFF and no security
ble_219_0c04bd48.description: Sets the 32-bit word at 0x2000FCAC to 0x00010001 and registers PSM 1 (SDP) with l2cap_register_service, MTU 0xFFFF, security level 0 and the handler context LAB_0C04C374. The 0x00010001 value is not identified; it may be two initial 16-bit fields. The name follows the BTstack sdp_init() convention for this registration, and the caller is 0x0C059230.

returns.description: none
